name: single-adjudicator-variance
whyThisM: 20 runs. For a function proved pure by reading it, M>=2 is the proof and the rest are the same proof again; 20 clean runs bound an unseen per-run divergence rate at only ~15% (rule of three). The inspection is the evidence here, not the count, and reporting the count as the evidence would overstate it.
batchProvenance: every open issue on hornjason/pai-harness at 2026-10-23T14:21:10.300Z, read through `openFindings` (the gate's own reader, capped at OPEN_ISSUE_LIMIT), each replayed as a fresh filing against the set with its own row held out, plus three plants.
caveat: The pinned arm's zero is zero BY CONSTRUCTION — `adjudicateFiling` is regex plus set arithmetic, with no clock, no randomness, no network and no model. Read it as a control establishing that the deterministic half contributes no variance, never as evidence that a quorum has nothing to fix. And the live arm's zero is bounded by its span (34.4s): M reads taken back to back cannot catch a tracker that moves on the scale of tens of minutes, so `distinctTrackerSets: 1` here is a control on the API read and NOT a measurement of tracker drift. Measuring that needs an hours-long window, which is a separate capture and was not taken — deliberately, because a window that long would likely straddle a merge to `lib/issue-filing-gate.ts` and measure a mixture.
permanentlyUnmeasured: No agent verifier feeds THIS gate. `arbitrate` has no caller outside lib/ and test/, and only `scripts/arbitrate-finding.ts` can supply `--votes`, so the verifier group a quorum would be a variance control for does not run on the filing path and is not read here.

A deployed agent verifier does exist elsewhere — the `ai-review` workflow — and its run-to-run variance IS now partly read, so this entry states a measurement rather than an absence. 1 same-tree pair(s) carry two verdicts with the tree, head, round and prompt all held fixed, and 1 of them DISAGREED: run 39962683401 returned BLOCKED then CLEAN on 99d50fc. A verdict flip is the failure a quorum is for, and it is the one reading here taken on a verifier that actually ships. Two cautions the number does not carry on its own. The turn counts across that flip were 51 and 52 — so `num_turns` is a poor proxy for verifier variance, and a stability argument built on turn counts is measuring the wrong quantity. And 2 of 3 same-tree pair(s) carry NO verdict — 1 because the round changed between attempts (an unequal round is a different prompt, not a repeat), and the rest because GitHub retained only the aggregate log. Those are UNMEASURED and are not attempts that agreed. n is small enough that no rate should be read off it; what it establishes is that the rate is not zero.

A withheld candidate leaves no trace on either arm. It is never filed, never commented on and never fixed, so nothing downstream records whether withholding it was right. `outcomes.ts` derives from commits and the reference graph; a candidate that reached neither is invisible to it, permanently.
A finding nobody ever acted on leaves no trace either — the same hole from the other side. There is no artefact to read, so this is not a measurement that is merely expensive.
